front: What do gastrocnemius and soleus have in common, and what's the key difference?
back: Both plantarflex the ankle and share the Achilles tendon insertion; only gastrocnemius also crosses the knee (and flexes it).

front: Why does a bent-knee calf stretch target soleus more than gastrocnemius?
back: Bending the knee slackens gastrocnemius (which crosses the knee), putting more stretch demand on soleus (which doesn't cross the knee).

What interesting anatomical relationship exists between tibialis anterior and peroneus longus?
back: They insert at nearly the same spot (base of 1st metatarsal/medial cuneiform) from opposite directions, forming a functional 'stirrup' supporting the foot arch.

front: 'Drop foot' (inability to dorsiflex) points to a problem with which muscle or its nerve?
Why is strengthening the peroneals often part of rehab after an inversion ankle sprain?
back: Peroneals (evertors) resist the inward-rolling motion that caused the injury.

front: Which muscle flexes the big toe and also helps support the arch of the foot?
Why do Achilles tendon issues potentially involve both gastrocnemius and soleus?
back: Both muscles share the Achilles tendon insertion onto the calcaneus.
